account:
Today has mostly followed my appointments: correspondence, a market walk, lunch, accounts, and afternoon tea at the neighbour's east-bank cottage. I now need to return to the office for 16:30. The treasury contains 128 emeralds, but I found no account papers, and the secretary has not located or verified the accounts. That is an administrative gap, not evidence of wrongdoing.

There are several unusual but inconclusive reports. Townsfolk repeatedly said the baker carried a sack of bread at the inn; I also saw the baker stock the market bread chest. Delivering bread to the inn could be ordinary business. My tea host heard talk of lights at the bakery, although the baker apparently knew of no celebration. The neighbour identifies Townsfolk 02 as the source of the phrase 'bridge or port change at bakery,' heard outside the bakery this morning. Others have repeated it without explaining it, and the neighbour saw no change personally. I have no confirmed riverfront project and cannot tell whether this phrase describes real work, a misunderstanding, or something else.

The builder has invited me to inspect the great hall lighting tomorrow at 18:00. The secretary says this is recorded and both appointment books are secured in the appointments chest. This is the only definite lighting-related plan I know; I cannot assume it explains bakery lights or the rumours. The secretary came to the cottage to ask where the account materials are, and says there is no known urgent business. Something may be being arranged without my knowing its purpose, but I have no evidence of a secret celebration or a coordinated scheme. I should keep my office appointment, clarify the accounts, and seek direct information rather than treat repeated gossip as fact.
